fields.meta_title: Photo Contest Form Builder With Blind Judging | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a photo contest form that caps photos per category and shows judges entry numbers, not names. Photos save to a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Photo Contest Form With Category Caps and Blind Judging
fields.hero_description: Build a photo contest form that takes each photo with its title and category, then shows judges entry numbers instead of names.
fields.features_heading: Entries Sorted Before the Judges Sit Down
fields.features_subheading: Describe your rules once, and Emergent builds a photo contest form that holds each entrant to them and gives judges a numbered set.
fields.feature_1:
A title and a category on every photo

Each upload carries a title and the category it enters, next to the entrant's name and email. Judges see what every photo is called and which category it belongs in.
fields.feature_2:
Entry limits for each category

Set how many photos one person may enter in a category. When someone reaches the limit in Nature, the form says so and offers the categories where they still have room.
fields.feature_3:
Judging by entry number, not name

The judges' screen shows each photo with its entry number and category. Names stay on the organizer's side, so a judge scoring a club friend's photo cannot tell it is theirs.
fields.feature_4:
A final round built from judges' stars

Each judge stars favorites on their own screen. Any photo with enough stars moves to the final round, and you set how many it takes, such as 2 stars from a panel of 3.
fields.feature_5:
Every entry in a database you own

Each entry becomes a row with the entrant, the email, the category, the photo, and its stars. Sort by stars to see the leaders, or filter to the photos no judge has opened yet.
fields.feature_6:
The code, exported to your GitHub

On paid plans, export the code for the form and the judges' screen to your GitHub repository. Host it with the rest of your club's site, or have a developer keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Clubs, Tourism Boards, Schools, and Rescues
fields.tab_content_1:
After 2 in Nature, Pauline's third photo goes to Monochrome

Kettle Rock Camera Club runs a monthly competition, and each member may enter 2 photos per category. Pauline Vashenko already has 2 heron shots in Nature for October. When she uploads a third, the form tells her Nature is full this month and offers Monochrome, where she has 0 entries. She enters it there as Fog Over the Weir.
fields.tab_content_2:
Every photo names its park, and Cobbler Falls leads at 41

The Tamarack County Visitors Bureau asks every entrant to pick the park where the photo was taken, from a list of 6. Its entry table counts all 188 photos by park. Cobbler Falls leads with 41 entries. Quarry Lake has the fewest, 22, and the bureau features it in the next newsletter.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 96 photos, 9 earn stars from 2 judges or more

Larch Valley High's art department received 96 photos for its spring contest. Three judges star favorites on a screen that shows entry numbers, never student names. Any photo starred by at least 2 judges goes to the final round. The final round holds 9 photos, led by entry 0583 with all 3 stars.
fields.tab_content_4:
Lisette chases February when it stalls at 3 entries

Cinderhill Animal Rescue is picking 12 photos for next year's calendar, one for each month. Every entrant chooses the month the photo suits. Of 140 entries so far, February has 3 and July has 4. Any month under 5 entries is flagged for Lisette Marrow, the volunteer coordinator, who posts a call for snowy February shots.

plan.angle: The AlsoAsked results for photo contests are entrant questions (where to submit, which contests are legit), so no result shows the organizer the form they need. This page shows the photo contest form a camera club, a tourism bureau, a school art department and an animal rescue each run: entry limits per category, a park picked on every entry, judging by entry number with a star shortlist, and a calendar contest that flags thin months.
tab_stories: Kettle Rock Camera Club allows 2 photos per category each month, so when Pauline Vashenko adds a third Nature photo the form says Nature is full for October and offers Monochrome, where she has entered none.
The Tamarack County Visitors Bureau has every entrant pick one of 6 parks, and its entry table groups the 188 photos by park: Cobbler Falls leads with 41 and Quarry Lake has the fewest at 22.

Larch Valley High's art department received 96 photos, 3 judges star favorites on a screen showing entry numbers instead of names, and the 9 photos starred by at least 2 judges reach the final round, led by entry 0583 with all 3 stars.
Cinderhill Animal Rescue is choosing 12 calendar photos, one per month, from 140 entries, and any month under 5 entries is flagged for Lisette Marrow, the coordinator: February has 3 and July has 4.
